evals.prompt: Create a Directus flow that sends a Slack notification whenever a new post is published
evals.expected_output: Complete flow with event trigger, condition, request operation, correct syntax
expectations: Creates flow with event trigger on items.create or items.update for posts
Creates condition operation checking status equals published
Uses nested object syntax for condition filter (not dot notation)
Creates request operation with POST to Slack webhook
Uses array format for request headers [{header, value}]
Uses stringified JSON for request body
Connects operations via resolve and sets flow entry point

evals.prompt: How do I reference data from the trigger in a Directus flow operation?
evals.expected_output: Data chain variables: $trigger, payload, keys, operation_key references
expectations: Lists $trigger variable and sub-paths (payload, keys, collection)
Explains operation key references ({{ operation_key }})
Warns against using $last
Shows nested object syntax for condition filters
Mentions stringified JSON for request body

evals.prompt: I need a Directus flow that sets archived=true on all old posts. My Update Items operation stopped changing anything after upgrading to 12.3
evals.expected_output: empty key/query returns null; explicit query with filter and limit -1
expectations: Explains that Update Items with an empty or missing key and query now returns null (Directus 12.3.0+)
Uses an explicit query with a filter and limit -1 for a bulk change
Warns that key and query together are an error
Notes that update by query applies read permissions (12.4.0+)

evals.prompt: Set up a Directus flow that tells my Next.js site to refresh its cache when a post is published, and keep the shared secret out of the URL.
evals.expected_output: Event flow with a request operation, secret in a header via $env and FLOWS_ENV_ALLOW_LIST
expectations: Uses an event trigger of type action on items.create, items.update and items.delete for the chosen collections
Uses a request operation with headers as an array of header/value objects and the body as a stringified JSON string
Sends the secret in a header, not in the query string
Reads the secret with {{ $env.NAME }} and explains FLOWS_ENV_ALLOW_LIST, noting the template renders undefined without it
Notes that localhost in the URL is the Directus container when Directus runs in Docker

evals.prompt: When an article is created or its body edited in Directus, my worker should process it. The worker writes ai_summary back into the same article and now the flow fires in a loop. Set up the flow so it sends the item ids to the worker and does not re-fire on the worker's own write.
evals.expected_output: Event flow with a request operation sending event, collection and keys; a condition with filter rules on $trigger.payload that the write-back does not satisfy; the secret in a header
expectations: Sends $trigger.keys, noting that it is always an array, in a stringified JSON body such as "keys":{{ $trigger.keys }}
Puts a condition operation before the request and writes it as filter rules in nested objects (for example $trigger.payload.body _nnull true), not as an expression string
Explains that on items.update the payload holds only the fields that request changed, so the worker's write-back (without the source field) fails the condition and the flow ends
Keeps the secret in a header read from $env with FLOWS_ENV_ALLOW_LIST, not in the URL
Says a Run Script (exec) operation cannot compute an HMAC (isolated context, no crypto or Node modules) and offers the header secret, a JWT operation or a custom operation
Tells the receiver to answer quickly and be idempotent, because the request operation does not retry and editors save repeatedly
